tytul: Pickled young honey fungus: why there is no recipe here
wstep: There is no recipe here for young honey fungus (opieńki) in a vinegar pickling liquid.

ostrzezenia.tekst: Drying and cooking do not destroy the toxins of poisonous mushrooms, and only an expert can tell edible species from poisonous ones.

akapity: NCHFP warns: do not can wild mushrooms; its tested canning process is only for small to medium-size cultivated mushrooms with unopened caps.
Mushrooms pickled in vinegar and processed in jars in a boiling-water bath are canned mushrooms, so this warning applies to them too.
The FDA list gives mushrooms a pH of about 6.00–6.70, while acid foods are foods with a natural pH of 4.6 or lower.
According to the Polish State Sanitary Inspection, honey fungus is an edible mushroom, but only young caps are fit to eat.

According to ATS Milano, a public health agency, honey fungus (Armillaria mellea) is toxic raw or undercooked; to make it edible it must first be boiled for at least 20 minutes without a lid and the water thrown away, because it contains toxins that are inactivated by heat.
JarAtlas has found no tested recipe for wild mushrooms in vinegar from a checked source.
